ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the current I in the conductor is marked with an arrow, with the direction along the conductor to the right; the magnetic flux density B is represented by several arrows slanting upward, located near the side surface of the conductor, and the problem statement indicates that its direction is perpendicular to the side surface of the conductor; on the right side, the potential difference V measured between the upper and lower surfaces is marked with a bracket; on the left side, the conductor thickness D is marked; the conductor cross-sectional area is marked as S. Reasoning: Let the Hall spacing between the upper and lower surfaces be h, then the cross-sectional area S = D h. The Hall coefficient is defined as R_H = E_H/(jB). Among them, the Hall electric field E_H = V/h, and the current density j = I/S = I/(D h). Substituting gives R_H = (V/h)/[(I/(D h))B] = VD/(IB).

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: identify I along the conductor, B perpendicular to the side surface, V across the top and bottom surfaces, and D as the conductor thickness so that S=D h for Hall-gap h. Then apply R_H=E_H/(jB), substitute E_H=V/h and j=I/S, and use S=D h to obtain R_H=VD/(IB).
